title: Keyturn Vehicle Listing: Booking an Odometer Reading against the Inspection Interval
content:
Where the marketplace has taken an odometer reading on a vehicle offered as a Keyturn Vehicle Listing, the reading is booked against that vehicle's inspection mileage credit. One entry carries the reading, where the reading came from, the condition record it was taken from, and the miles that reading takes off the interval, which are booked to the vehicle's inspection mileage credit as a deduction of that size. The listing's class, price and standing are untouched; what the desk and the host see afterwards is an odometer entry dated today with the miles it consumed.

The reading booked is recorded through the channel the completed inspection it is taken from was carried out under, since the reading the marketplace books is that inspection's own.

### Making the entry

The desk unlocks the agent-side tool `record_booked_mileage_82af4bea` and calls it. One call books one reading.

### Parameters

- `vehicle_id` — the listing reference number of the vehicle the reading belongs to, read from the vehicle listing lookup before the call.
- `customer_id` — the member reference number of the host who owns that listing, read from the member profile lookup before the call.
- `source_inspection_id` — the reference number of the condition record the reading is taken from; that reference number is carried on the record itself and is repeated in any receipt that reports it.
- `odometer_reading` — the odometer being booked, in whole miles as an integer, with no decimal part, no unit suffix and no thousands separator.
- `inspection_channel` — where the reading came from, exactly one of: `self_photo`, the host photographed the odometer themselves; `partner_shop`, a partner workshop read the odometer while holding the vehicle; `mobile_inspector`, a marketplace inspector read the odometer at the vehicle; `telematics_report`, the fitted telematics unit reported the odometer.
- `booked_miles_consumed` — the miles this reading takes off the vehicle's inspection interval, in whole miles as an integer, with no decimal part, no unit suffix and no thousands separator; it is booked to the inspection mileage credit as whole miles, signed, a negative deduction of the same size, and zero means the reading consumes nothing.

### What comes back

A confirmation sentence naming the reference number minted for the new odometer record, the listing it was booked against, the reading recorded and the miles taken off the interval. The presence of that reference number in the sentence is what indicates the reading now stands on the vehicle's condition record.
